algorithms.name: PatientBandits with input sequence alpha_t = log log t / log t

symbols.alpha_tail: delay tail exponent of Assumption 1: |1 - tau_i(m)| <= m^(-alpha_tail)

source.label: thm:pbdep
source.quote: Let $T> K \geq 1 $ and $\alpha>0$. Let $((\mathcal{V}_i, \cD_i)_{i\in[K]})$ be the problem as defined in Section~\ref{sec:setting} such that Assumption~\ref{as:alpha} holds. If  $\DelUCB$ is run with parameters $\cP = (\alpha, T,K)$, it achieves \overline{R}_T \leq \sum _{i: \Delta_i>0}  \Big[\frac{64 \log(2T)}{\Delta_i}  \lor \Big(\frac{8}{\Delta_i}\Big)^{\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha} \lor 1}\Big] + 2K.

results.notes: Regret defined as sum_i Delta_i E[T_i(T)], i.e. pseudo-regret. alpha renamed alpha_tail to avoid clash with canonical strong-convexity alpha.

source.label: thm:pbindep
source.quote: Let $T> K \geq 1 $ and $\alpha>0$. If $\DelUCB$ is run with parameters $\cP=(\alpha, T,K)$, for any \emph{stochastic delayed problem} such that Assumption~\ref{as:alpha} holds, it achieves \overline{R}_T \leq  2\times 64^{(1-\alpha) \lor 1/2} T^{1 - \alpha \land 1/2}\Big(K\log(2T) \Big)^{\alpha \land 1/2} +2K.

results.notes: Order max(sqrt(KT), K^alpha T^(1-alpha)) up to logs.

conditions: hard instance: delays mass p=T^(-alpha_tail) at T for the best arm

source.label: thm:lbreg
source.quote: Consider $K = 2$ and $T\geq K$, and $\alpha>0$. There exists a Bernoulli stochastic delayed bandit problem satisfying Assumption~\ref{as:alpha}, such that the expected regret of any algorithm $\bar R_T$ on this problem is larger than $T^{1 - \alpha}/8.$

results.notes: Expected regret as defined in eq. (regret) = sum Delta_i E T_i, i.e. pseudo-regret.

bound.regime: T > e^{e^e}, log log T / log T <= min_i alpha_i, 8/Delta_min <= log T

tuning: input sequence alpha_t = log log t / log t

source.label: thm:lbreg2
source.quote: Consider $K = 2,$ $T\geq K,$ and fix $\alpha >0$. For any $\beta \geq  \alpha,$ there exists a Bernoulli bandit instance satisfying Assumption~\ref{as:alpha} for $\beta$ such that the expected regret $\bar R_T$ of any $\alpha$-optimal algorithm is larger than $T^{1 -  \alpha}/8>T^{1-\beta}/8.$

results.notes: Impossibility of adaptation result; restricted algorithm class.

source.quote: Let $T> K \geq 1 $ and $\alpha, \underline{\alpha}, c,  \bar\mu >0, $ such that Assumption~\ref{as:alph2} holds. The expected regret of $\aDelUCB$ is bounded as $R_T = \tcO(K^\alpha T^{1-\alpha \land \nicefrac{1}{2}})$.

results.notes: Full version in Theorem 7 (appendix) has exponent alpha ∧ 1/2 on K.
